item.title: iacula — The End of Ages Archive
item.description:
iacula: The End of Ages Archive

Website: iacula.com
Role: Author Architecture, Multi-Volume Lore Structuring, Reader Experience
Stack: Hugo custom theme (iacula-blank), dual content mounts, RSS feeds, static distribution

The Visual Problem

The End of Ages is a four-book epic fantasy cycle developed over sixteen years. Author websites for extensive fantasy fiction frequently struggle to balance promotional publication announcements with the deep lore, histories, and world documentation demanded by devoted readers.

The brief called for an author platform that speaks from within the world itself: scholarly, atmospheric, and capable of housing extensive lore volumes alongside publication dates and book purchase channels.

item.title: Nox — Architecture for a Literary House
item.description:
Nox: Architecture for a Literary House

Website: arxnox.com
Role: Design, Information Architecture, Static Engineering
Stack: Bespoke Hugo architecture, Markdown ledger, Custom RSS feeds, Zero runtime dependencies

The Visual Problem

Nox is the central publishing house representing several distinct writing voices and genres. Most multi-author or publishing websites resemble cluttered ecommerce stores or generic blog feeds: rotating hero banners, newsletter popups, cookie consent overlays, and complex content management systems that slow down page delivery.

item.title: selador — Digital Art on an Obsidian Canvas
item.description:
selador: Digital Art on an Obsidian Canvas

Website: selador.art
Role: Visual Design, Gallery System, Deployment Architecture
Stack: Custom minimalist theme (selador-blank), static build, origin media delivery

The Visual Problem

Contemporary art portfolio platforms are burdened by two failure modes:

  1. Proprietary portfolio builders that enforce cookie notices, watermark overlays, and generic grid templates.
  2. Third-party marketplace platforms that take substantial commission cuts and subject visitors to advertising, analytics, and social distraction.

The artist behind selador required a digital gallery that functions like a physical viewing room with dark walls and focused directional lighting: completely silent, respectful of high-resolution image rendering, and distraction-free.
